units.text: INT. APPELLATE COURTROOM - LOBBY - DAY
A marble anteroom, high-windowed, quiet as a chapel.
A bench, a water cooler, a brass door that gives onto the courtroom proper.
CASSIUS WELLINGTON-OBI stands at the window with his back to the room, a man of fifty with a brief clutched against his chest.
ADA LOVELACE-REYES sits on the bench with her ankles crossed, composed in a blue suit.
Between them, a younger associate, THEO SANDOVAL, shifts from foot to foot.
She does not look up when he speaks.
He doesn't turn when she answers.
Ms. Lovelace-Reyes, the panel's been out forty minutes.
units.name: THEO

units.text: Forty-one.
units.name: ADA

units.text: Forty-two.
units.name: CASSIUS

units.text: That's a good sign, right? Long means they're reading everything.
units.name: THEO

units.text: Long means they're arguing.
units.name: ADA

units.text: Long means nothing.
units.name: CASSIUS

units.text: So it's a bad sign.
units.name: THEO

units.text: It's not a sign.
units.name: ADA

units.text: He wipes his palms on his trousers.
She straightens a cuff.
He turns from the window at last and takes a single step into the room.
Ada, when you're done being calm, I'd appreciate it if you'd tell me what it is we've forgotten.
units.name: CASSIUS

units.text: We've forgotten nothing.
units.name: ADA

units.text: Then why am I sweating?
units.name: CASSIUS

units.text: Because the AC's broken.
units.name: THEO

units.text: The brass door swings open.
A clerk looks out and calls them in.
The three of them stand together.
Nobody moves toward the door until Ada does.
